prompt:
Create a single publication-quality landscape 3:2 narrative illustration for an adult illustrated English-reading booklet. Finished standalone artwork, not a book mockup, not a collage of multiple unrelated panels. Sophisticated contemporary editorial gouache and watercolor, carefully controlled colored-pencil accents, velvety matte paint, subtle warm paper texture, soft natural daylight. Warm ivory paper dominates; subdued eucalyptus and sage greens structure the composition; restrained buttery lemon-yellow and dusty terracotta accents. Calm, comfortable, refined, credible drawing and natural anatomy. An airy coherent composition with one clear story focal point and at most two supporting details, generous breathing room at all edges and softly feathered painted edges into ivory. Detailed but uncluttered. Historically and scientifically appropriate objects, clothing and setting. Show the particular article's pivotal event or mechanism rather than a generic portrait or generic textbook symbols. Human figures treated with dignity; no grotesque caricature, no sensational violence or visible injuries. For disasters, emphasize the setting, evidence or human response without graphic suffering. For uncertain scientific claims, depict the observations and investigation without presenting debated mechanisms as proven. Absolutely no typography, captions, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, diagram labels, fake writing or invented charts anywhere. Do not render invisible forces as literal magic. Avoid corporate vector icons, slick 3D rendering and childish cartoon style. High-quality, print-ready visual storytelling, matching a warm ivory-and-sage adult watercolor booklet.

ARTICLE-SPECIFIC SCENE: A coherent still life on a modest late-1980s publishing-office meeting table: an unbranded upright gray pocket handheld game console, inspired by the original Game Boy, is the clear focal object. The console has a large muted-green monochrome screen, a simple cross-shaped direction pad and two plain dark terracotta round buttons with no letters. On screen show only a few simple falling geometric clusters, each composed of exactly four square cells, and a sparse bottom stack; absolutely no scores, interface text or logos. One plain black floppy disk and a small stack of completely blank licensing papers are the only supporting objects, linking Soviet software circulation with the later handheld-rights deal. The scene evokes the move from floppy copies to a mass-market pocket game, not a fake historical photograph or a collage. Do not show the Elektronika 60 displaying colorful graphics, and do not print character-based screens because no typography is allowed. Natural soft window light, warm ivory paper, sage display, restrained terracotta accents.
review_notes: 已查看修订后的实际输出：单独下落的图形为清楚可数的四格T形（横三格、中下一格）；保留单色掌机、软盘与空白授权文件。初图三格缺陷已用imagegen修复，未用Python改图；人物与手部自然，无品牌文字。画面为版权与掌机传播的编辑性示意，不指认为某次谈判的实景。
edit_prompt: Edit this exact illustration and preserve its adult warm-ivory/sage gouache-watercolor style, characters, hands, console body, tabletop, lighting and blank papers. Correct ONE precise factual error on the handheld console screen: the isolated falling piece currently has only THREE little square cells. Replace that isolated falling piece with a clearly outlined T-shaped tetromino made of EXACTLY FOUR equally sized square cells: THREE cells in a straight horizontal row, PLUS ONE cell directly below the middle cell. The result must visibly show four individual outlined cells, no ambiguity and no extra cell. Leave the bottom stack otherwise unchanged. Keep the whole screen monochrome sage-green. Absolutely no letters, numbers, logos, scores or labels; this is a plain four-square geometric game shape. Make the revised falling piece slightly larger if needed so all four outlined cells can be counted clearly. Do not change anything else.
